record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For an isolated complete intersection singularity ϕ with two-dimensional base space and the embedded-resolution local setup that restricts V(ϕ) to a Z^2-variation structure near a point P on the exceptional divisor, a natural limit mixed Hodge structure carries a Z^2 action via the semisimple part of the monodromy representation. Can the isolated-hypersurface theorem connecting the topological invariant V(f) with the Hodge-theoretical primitive invariants pλ^{a,b}(f), and in particular showing that Hodge numbers determine the real Seifert form, be extended to this Z^2 limit mixed-Hodge setting?

evidence.quote: The connection between the topological invariant V(f ) and the Hodge theoretical invariants pλa,b (f ) is given in the following Theorem.[11]
In particular, the Hodge numbers determine the real Seifert form.

Problem # 5. In the context of Problem # 4 there is a natural limit mixed Hodge structure with the action of Z2 (via the semi–simple part of the monodromy representation) ([19], see also [15] and [17]). Extend the above Theorem to this case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\phi:(\mathbb{C}^{n+2},0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ be the germ of an isolated complete intersection singularity with two-dimensional base. Choose an embedded resolution of the discriminant and fix a point $P$ on the exceptional divisor where two smooth components meet transversally. Restricting the geometric vanishing data of $\phi$ to a small bidisc transverse to the exceptional divisor at $P$ yields a $\mathbb{Z}^2$-variation structure $V(\phi)$ on the local vanishing cohomology, in the sense of Némethi: a free $\mathbb{Z}$-module equipped with two commuting monodromy automorphisms, two variation maps, an intersection form and a Seifert-type form, satisfying the usual compatibility relations.

Hodge side. The two commuting monodromies $h_1,h_2$ act on the vanishing cohomology, and one has a natural limit mixed Hodge structure (a polarized bigraded $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant analog of Steenbrink's limit mixed Hodge structure) on which the semisimple parts of $h_1,h_2$ act, decomposing the cohomology into joint eigenspaces indexed by pairs of eigenvalues $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in(\mathbb{C}^*)^2$. From this one extracts primitive Hodge numbers $p^{a,b}_\lambda(\phi)$ ($a,b\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, $\lambda\in(\mathbb{C}^*)^2$) refining Steenbrink's spectrum.

Hypersurface model. In the one-parameter (isolated hypersurface singularity $f$) case, the following is known: the integral $\mathbb{Z}$-variation structure $V(f)$, after tensoring with $\mathbb{R}$, is completely determined by the primitive equivariant Hodge numbers $p^{a,b}_\lambda(f)$; in particular these Hodge numbers determine the real Seifert form of $f$.

Problem. Prove or disprove the analogous statement for $\phi$: do the primitive equivariant Hodge numbers $p^{a,b}_\lambda(\phi)$ of the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant limit mixed Hodge structure determine the real $\mathbb{Z}^2$-variation structure $V(\phi)\otimes\mathbb{R}$, and in particular the real Seifert form attached to $\phi$ at $P$?
artifact.category_tag: Variation structures and limit mixed Hodge structures of singularities
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., Kulikov–Némethi and Hertling–Stahlke on real Seifert forms and Steenbrink mixed Hodge structures, 2017–2020) confirm and refine the hypersurface theorem relating Hodge numbers to the real Seifert form, but no search result explicitly establishes the analogous statement for the $\mathbb{Z}^2$-equivariant limit mixed Hodge structure of an isolated complete intersection singularity with two-dimensional base. The status of the extension to this $\mathbb{Z}^2$ setting could not be confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Real Seifert forms and polarizing forms of Steenbrink mixed Hodge structures
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of irreducible Seifert form pairs and polarizing forms on generalized eigenspaces for isolated hypersurface singularities.
status_evidence.claim: The hypersurface case (one monodromy) of the theorem to be extended has been treated in detail.

status_evidence.title: Real Seifert forms, Hodge numbers and Blanchfield pairings
status_evidence.snippet: Hermitian Variation Structures introduced by Némethi connect Picard-Lefschetz invariants of isolated hypersurface singularities with Hodge-theoretic data.
status_evidence.claim: Variation structure / Hodge number connection is established for hypersurfaces; ICIS Z^2 extension not addressed.
